label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 2 generates four purpose rows in one drawer, with one negative-purpose statement, three entry gateway choices, three final gateway choices, no reset traps, no directed links, and stationary gateways.

Full interaction uses direct clicks on the gateway cards, the ledger review button, and pointer drags on each purpose switch rail between NO and YES; the single drawer has no meaningful navigation choice.
The exact task settings are a 720 ms observation window with five frames per observation and 180 seconds of maximum task-active time.
autonomous_processes: While a gateway stage is visible, requestAnimationFrame repeatedly updates the packet timer and recomputes each card position. With moving_gateways=false, the phase is constant, so the card positions and stacking remain constant.
While the preferences ledger is visible, the same animation-frame loop continues updating the packet timer, but purpose states, drawer state, and available controls change only from input handlers.
The shared clock advances performance.now during live run windows and freezes it while paused; this supplies task-clock progress but no outcome-affecting autonomous transition in this configuration.
grouped_control_modes: Full direct gateway-card clicks, grouped across the entry manage choice and final commit choice (with randomized semantic decoys).
Full pointer drags on purpose switch rails, across the four generated purpose rows.

clause_i.reason: The relevant controls remain available after waiting, so an observation-free wait/no-op schedule can defer the static semantic choice to a later optimal continuation. The randomized labels and initial switch values create a static visual-grounding problem, not a need to choose from changing state.

clause_ii.reason: A current screenshot is sufficient: the visible gateway labels identify the manage/commit choice, and the visible purpose text plus switch state identify the required full-mode drag. A zero-length recent window would suffice; the configured 720 ms window and five frames are more than enough.

clause_iii.reason: No non-clock autonomous evolution makes an available action unavailable or less effective. With moving_gateways=false, currentPhase ignores elapsed time and positionOrbit writes the same card coordinates on each frame; the timer is the only changing display. Purpose states and stages change only in response to clicks/drags, and difficulty 2 has no reset traps or links. The 180-second limit is only a clock/deadline effect, which the definition excludes.

common_visible_process: None. The continuously changing packet timer is unrelated to the outcome, while the gateway geometry is stationary; therefore no single visible autonomous process witnesses clauses (i), (ii), and (iii).

pre_run.reason: The configuration already fails the mathematical real-time definition because there is no autonomous outcome phase with an expiring or degrading action opportunity. The pre-run threshold cannot change that No label, so no percentage is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: The assigned difficulty-2 profile is purpose_count 4, negative_count 1, drawer_count 1, three entry and final options, zero reset/link controls, moving_gateways false, and orbit speed 0.
Full mode is implemented as direct gateway-card clicks, ledger-tab interaction, and physical switch drags; the shared settings are 180 seconds, 720 ms, and five frames.
The generator takes difficulty parameters from the control condition and otherwise defines the baseline separately; the assigned control condition therefore determines the active profile.
Purpose labels and initial boolean states are generated per seed, while positive and negative labels determine the target state; this is static instance variation.
The generated surface contains entry/final gateway options, purposes, reset traps, links, and one static phase value; at difficulty 2 the latter controls no motion.
currentPhase adds elapsed time only when moving_gateways is true; positionOrbit changes the packet timer and recalculates card coordinates on each frame.
Stage rendering and purpose/link state changes are invoked by action handlers; there is no autonomous mutation of the ledger state.
Full-mode purpose changes require a pointer drag with movement samples and minimum travel, confirming the active physical control surface.
Gateway clicks, full-mode drawer/switch bindings, review transition, and the per-run timer state are wired as explicit user-event handlers.
Gateway cards are absolutely positioned visual controls with no CSS motion rule; their runtime positions come from the JavaScript phase calculation.
The preferences surface presents static NO/YES rails, pointer-drag styling, and the review button; no difficulty-2 reset control is active.
The grader only adds elapsed-time phase to moving gateways; for a stationary profile it uses the fixed surface phase and validates static geometry.
The grader replays gateway events and stage transitions from the submitted transcript, rather than advancing any autonomous task state.
Purpose, link, reset, review, and final success state are changed/replayed only when corresponding events occur; task time is only ordered and bounded.
The solver actively clicks manage, sets visible purpose switches, reviews, and clicks commit; there is no autonomous outcome phase to run without further outcome-affecting actions.
performance.now is virtualized to task time, and the separate interaction clock is for input evidence while timers/animation/physics remain on the task clock.
When paused, task-time timers and queued animation callbacks do not advance; live windows resume the task clock.

The frozen definition requires one visibly evidenced autonomous process that degrades an action opportunity; static puzzles, idle animation, clock-only effects, and indefinitely actionable controls are excluded.
